newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik govt vows to crush maverick rebel leader.
newsitem.headline: Tajik govt vows to crush maverick rebel leader.

text.p: Tajikistan's government said on Thursday it planned to destroy an armed group led by maverick fighter and hostage-taker Rizvon Sadirov.
"The Tajik government has started an operation to annihilate terrorists led by field commander Rizvon Sadirov," presidential spokesman Zafar Saidov told Reuters.
"The fighters have refused to lay down their weapons," Saidov said, in reference to a government ultimatum issued to Sadirov on Wednesday.
He said the operation was taking place around 80 km (50 miles) east of the capital Dushanbe but gave no further details.
Sadirov once fought for Tajikistan's Islamic opposition against the secular government of the mountainous former Soviet republic but his loyalties are now unclear.

Last December, his fighters seized a group of foreigners working in Tajikistan. In February, Sadirov's brother Bakhrom held 14 international aid workers, foreign military observers and Russian journalists for nearly two weeks.
The brothers demanded free passage for their men to return to the country from bases in neighbouring Afghanistan. The government bowed to all conditions.

The maverick brothers have proved important politically in the chronically unstable country as the government joined forces with units of the country's Islamic opposition -- its former foes in a bitter four-year civil war -- to hunt them down.

Last December, the secular government and the opposition agreed a ceasefire which seems to be holding and are hammering out details of a new power-sharing arrangement. Bakhrom Sadirov and around 20 of his men were arrested and brought to Dushanbe at the weekend.
